scene_translation: Stepping out of Shinjuku Station's south exit, the fading evening light melted softly between the buildings. Just as you were about to be swallowed by the flow of people, you noticed a white envelope lying at your feet. Picking it up, you saw written on the front in handwriting: 'To テスト-sama.' Opening the envelope, inside was a single sheet of paper that read only: 'Before night falls, visit the old clock shop at the west exit.' Looking around, the person who left this letter was nowhere to be found.
grammar_note: 【〜前に】means 'before ~' and attaches to the dictionary form of a verb. Here: 「<ruby>夜<rt>よる</rt></ruby>になる<ruby>前<rt>まえ</rt></ruby>に」= 'before it becomes night.' The verb before 前に is always in its plain (dictionary) form, even when the main sentence is in polite ます/です style.

mystery_memo: The central mystery begins: a white envelope addressed to the player by name (テスト) was waiting at Shinjuku Station south exit — no sender visible. The note inside directs the player to an old clock shop at the west exit before nightfall. Key question: who knew the player's name and arrival? The clock shop is the next destination. Player has the letter; its contents and the identity of the sender are the first threads to pull.
